message.content:
I need to find where memo-derived metadata is computed from memo content in this repository. This is metadata used for lists/previews that is automatically extracted from the memo's content rather than set by the user. Search for:

1. Any function or method that computes/extracts metadata from memo content (e.g., snippet, title, excerpt, summary, preview text)
2. Look for patterns like "snippet", "excerpt", "preview", "metadata", "derived" in relation to memos
3. Check for any content parsing that extracts properties like title, description, or similar from memo body/content

Search breadth: very thorough. Look across the entire codebase for memo-related metadata computation. Check store files, service files, helper/utility files, and API handlers.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me provide the final report.

---

Here is a thorough accounting of every location where memo-derived metadata is computed from memo content in this repository.

## 1. Core Metadata Extraction Engine

**File: `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`**

This is the central markdown service that all metadata extraction flows through. It defines the `Service` interface (line 31) with these key methods:

### a) `ExtractAll` (line 356) -- The primary single-pass extractor
Parses memo markdown content once and extracts in a single AST walk:
- **Tags** (`[]string`): All `#tag` nodes found in content (deduplicated, case-preserving)
- **Mentions** (`[]string`): All `@mention` nodes (lowercased, deduplicated)
- **Property** (`*storepb.MemoPayload_Property`): A struct containing:
  - `Title` (string): Plain text of the first H1 heading if it is the very first block-level child of the document (lines 383-389)
  - `HasLink` (bool): Whether any markdown link exists (line 393)
  - `HasCode` (bool): Whether code blocks or inline code spans exist (line 396)
  - `HasTaskList` (bool): Whether GFM task checkboxes exist (line 399)
  - `HasIncompleteTasks` (bool): Whether any unchecked task checkboxes exist (lines 400-403)

The return type is `ExtractedData` (line 21):
```go
type ExtractedData struct {
    Tags     []string
    Mentions []string
    Property *storepb.MemoPayload_Property
}
```

### b) `ExtractProperties` (line 193) -- Properties-only extraction
Same property computation as `ExtractAll` but does not extract tags or mentions. Used when only properties are needed.

### c) `ExtractTags` (line 143) -- Tags-only extraction
Extracts only `#tag` nodes from the AST.

### d) `GenerateSnippet` (line 264) -- Plain-text snippet generation
Walks the AST to produce a plain-text summary:
- Strips all markdown formatting (bold, italic, etc.)
- Skips code blocks entirely (but preserves inline code text)
- Collapses block elements (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells) with single spaces
- Includes tag nodes as `#tagname`, autolinks as their URL text, image alt text
- Truncates at a word boundary if the result exceeds `maxLength` runes, appending ` ...`

### e) `extractHeadingText` (line 173) / `extractTextFromNode` (line 182)
Helper functions that recursively extract plain text from a heading node (stripping inline formatting like bold/italic), used by `ExtractProperties` and `ExtractAll` for title extraction.

### f) `truncateAtWord` (line 472)
Truncates a string at the last word boundary before `maxLength` (counted in runes, not bytes) and appends ` ...`.

## 2. Payload Rebuild Runner (Batch Re-extraction)

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`**

### `RebuildMemoPayload` (line 74)
Called on every memo create and content update. Invokes `markdownService.ExtractAll()` on `memo.Content` and writes the results back to `memo.Payload`:
```go
memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
```

### `RunOnce` (line 27)
A batch runner that iterates all memos in the database (in batches of 100), calls `RebuildMemoPayload` on each, and persists the updated payload. Used for backfill/migration.

## 3. Snippet Generation at API Layer

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`**

### `getMemoContentSnippet` (line 83)
A thin wrapper on the APIV1Service that calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(content, 64)` -- producing a max-64-character plain-text snippet. This is the single entry point for snippet generation across the API layer.

## 4. Memo Conversion (Store -> API Response)

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`**

### `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` (line 31)
The main conversion function that builds a `v1pb.Memo` API response from a `store.Memo`. It:
- Copies `memo.Payload.Tags` -> `memoMessage.Tags` (line 48)
- Calls `convertMemoPropertyFromStore(memo.Payload.Property)` -> `memoMessage.Property` (line 49)
- Calls `s.getMemoContentSnippet(memo.Content)` -> `memoMessage.Snippet` (lines 76-80)

### `convertMemoPropertyFromStore` (line 315)
Maps the stored protobuf property to the API protobuf property:
```go
func convertMemoPropertyFromStore(property *storepb.MemoPayload_Property) *v1pb.Memo_Property {
    return &v1pb.Memo_Property{
        HasLink:            property.HasLink,
        HasTaskList:        property.HasTaskList,
        HasCode:            property.HasCode,
        HasIncompleteTasks: property.HasIncompleteTasks,
        Title:              property.Title,
    }
}
```

### `batchConvertMemoRelations` (line 173)
When building relation objects for memo list responses, it optionally generates snippets for each related memo by calling `s.getMemoContentSnippet(m.Content)`. The snippets are placed on `MemoRelation.Memo.Snippet` and `MemoRelation.RelatedMemo.Snippet` (lines 269, 273).

## 5. Memo Create & Update Flows

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`**

### CreateMemo (line 108)
Calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService)` before persisting -- this extracts tags, title, and boolean properties from the new memo's content.

### UpdateMemo (line 447)
When the `content` field is in the update mask, calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService)` to re-extract metadata from the updated content, then persists `memo.Payload`.

## 6. Notification Snippet

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`**

### `memoNotificationSnippet` (line 318)
Generates a snippet for inbox/notification payloads by calling `s.getMemoContentSnippet(memo.Content)`.

## 7. Mention Extraction

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`**

### `resolveMentionTargets` (line 26)
Calls `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll(content)` to get `data.Mentions` -- the list of `@username` references extracted from memo content. Used to dispatch mention notification inbox items.

## 8. RSS Feed Title & Description

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go`**

### `generateItemTitle` (line 302)
Extracts the first line of memo content as the RSS item title:
- Takes the first line of the raw content string
- Strips markdown heading syntax (`# `, `## `, etc.) using regex
- Truncates at 100 characters on a word boundary, appending `...`
- Falls back to `"Memo"` if the result is empty

### `getRSSItemDescription` (line 338)
Renders memo content to HTML using `s.MarkdownService.RenderHTML(content)` for the RSS item description/content.

## 9. Link Metadata (External URL, Not Memo Content)

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go`**

This is related but distinct -- it fetches metadata (title, description, image) from external URLs found in memo content, not from the memo content itself. The actual HTML meta extraction is in:

**File: `/bench/home/work/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go`**
- `GetHTMLMeta` (line 136) / `extractHTMLMeta` (line 160): Parses HTML `<title>`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, and `<meta name="description">` from external URLs.

## 10. Protobuf Definitions

**File: `/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto`** -- Storage layer schema:
- `MemoPayload.Property` (line 15): `has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title`
- `MemoPayload.tags` (line 13)

**File: `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`** -- API layer schema:
- `Memo.tags` (line 241): `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `Memo.property` (line 256): `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `Memo.snippet` (line 266): `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `Memo.Property` (line 272): `has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title`
- `MemoRelation.Memo.snippet` (line 444): `OUTPUT_ONLY`

## 11. Frontend Consumption

The frontend does not compute memo-derived metadata itself -- it receives the server-computed fields (`snippet`, `property`, `tags`) and renders them. Key consumption points:
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoView/components/MemoSnippetLink.tsx` -- renders snippet text in relation links
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoDetailSidebar/MemoDetailSidebar.tsx` -- displays relation snippets in the sidebar
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoMetadata/Relation/RelationCard.tsx` -- renders relation card with snippet
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/UserMemoMap/UserMemoMap.tsx` -- displays snippet on map popups
- `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoMetadata/Relation/useResolvedRelationMemos.ts` -- hydrates missing snippets for relations

## Summary of Derived Metadata Fields

| Field | Source | Computed By | Where Stored |
|-------|--------|-------------|-------------|
| `tags` | `#tag` nodes in content | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractTags` | `memo.Payload.Tags` |
| `title` | First H1 heading text | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | `memo.Payload.Property.Title` |
| `has_link` | Presence of markdown links | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | `memo.Payload.Property.HasLink` |
| `has_code` | Presence of code blocks/spans | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | `memo.Payload.Property.HasCode` |
| `has_task_list` | Presence of GFM task checkboxes | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | `memo.Payload.Property.HasTaskList` |
| `has_incomplete_tasks` | Unchecked task checkboxes | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | `memo.Payload.Property.HasIncompleteTasks` |
| `snippet` | Plain-text summary (max 64 chars) | `GenerateSnippet` | Computed at API response time, not persisted |
| `mentions` | `@username` nodes in content | `ExtractAll` | Used ephemerally for notifications, not persisted in payload |
| RSS `title` | First line of content | `generateItemTitle` | Computed at RSS generation time |
